reviews.text: I had a very good experience. The staff and the veterinarians that work here are amazing and very helpful. They way the appointments are set help you don’t feel rushed and they actually do a full exam on your fur babies. They answers your questions and after your appointment you don’t leave feeling unsure about the visit going on with your fur baby. 10/10 recommend and I will definitely be going back.

If you are looking for a veterinarian in the Northridge, Chatsworth, Granada Hills or Porter Ranch area, especially if older Yelp reviews are making you hesitant, READ THIS. This practice is under new ownership and is now privately owned and operated by a veterinarian. My experience was completely different from what some older reviews describe.

I brought in Penelope, my 10-year-old German Shepherd and soul dog, who is currently undergoing chemotherapy for Stage IV B-cell lymphoma while also dealing with kidney disease and several chronic orthopedic and neurological conditions. Her medical history is extensive, and I came in with A LOT of questions.

They spent THREE HOURS with us.

Three hours reviewing her history, examining her, going through medications and diagnoses, answering questions, explaining their reasoning, and helping me understand what we should be watching for going forward. I have never received this level of attention from a veterinary practice.

The pricing is also remarkable. They are currently offering a two-week promotion with a $0 exam fee, and I was told the regular exam fee afterward will be approximately $75. Anyone paying veterinary bills in this area knows how reasonable that is.

The fact that this practice is independently owned also matters to me. I work in private equity and finance professionally, so I understand how ownership structure can influence revenue expectations, margins, staffing, cost controls and organizational culture. Those objectives make sense in many industries. I personally become more cautious when those financial incentives intersect with healthcare and living beings.

I never felt like Penelope was a number, a revenue opportunity or a list of billable diagnostics. I felt like she was a sick dog standing in front of people who genuinely wanted to help her.

What ultimately earned my trust wasn’t the price. It was their honesty.

During our appointment, they explained the specific changes that could indicate Penelope’s quality of life was deteriorating and that it might be time to discuss letting her go.

Initially, I was shocked. Then I realized it was probably the single most valuable thing anyone has told me since Penelope was diagnosed with cancer.

No one had ever explained it that directly. Not her oncologist, not previous veterinarians, no one. I knew some of it intuitively, but knowing something in your gut and having a medical professional compassionately give you concrete parameters to watch for are very different things.

Most importantly: How will I know when fighting for more time is no longer the same thing as fighting for her?

They explained what success could look like, what we could reasonably manage, what decline could look like, and what changes should trigger a serious quality-of-life conversation.

To me, that is compassion. Compassion isn’t always telling an owner everything will be okay. Sometimes it is caring enough about an animal to tell their owner something incredibly difficult BEFORE they are standing in the middle of a crisis.

This team understood that distinction. They were transparent about what was worthwhile, what information mattered, and what actually affected Penelope’s quality of life. I never felt pressured to spend money simply because another test or service was available.

Most importantly, I never felt like they saw a dollar sign when they looked at my dog. They saw Penelope.

So if older negative Yelp reviews concern you, look at the dates. I am reviewing the doctors, ownership and team who are there NOW, and my experience was exceptional.

Penelope’s medical records tell you how sick she is. They don’t tell you how much she still loves being alive. I need veterinarians who understand that difference. I found them here.

They have my business for the rest of Penelope’s life and, someday, they will have my business for my next dog’s life too.

I just want to thank the staff at PVC! Oso was so nervous for his nailtrim but Morgan and Robert? (Dont recall his name) made oso so comfortable. My oso is usually such an anxious wiggle worm but they gave him so much time and space that he didn't even cry. Thank you to Julianna who booked my appointment last min (I guess they just opened). But thank you all and I'm happy I found a better vet. Hello Dr. Ryan!

Too expensive. Dog had an open cut, and they charged a crazy amount for what it ended up being. They kept coming in and offering all these things I should do and of course I accepted bc it’s the health of the dog. I’ve been to other vets and have never been as expensive as this one.

I wanted to use my Care card so I could finance the expense but it happened to not be “set up.”

Would not recommend this place. There are more affordable and real places. They just want to sell you all there products so they can make money. Ridiculous.

Hope this place never opens again. Started going here regularly years ago and it was affordable and decent, but then it got steadily worse. Went from costing around $600 to have my dogs' teeth cleaned to $2000 in the span of two years. Last time we went, we pointed out the dog had a little growth on his side. Really just a little bump smaller than a pea. They said they would remove it during the tooth cleaning since he would be under. They didn't, and when I pointed it out, they said they forgot and it would cost another $2k to have ANOTHER surgery. I obviously did not have another $2k after paying a total of $6k to have all three dogs teeth cleaned. And what a surprise! That growth turned into a full blown gigantic tumor that killed my dog. So thanks, team at Porter Pet. Brilliant work. Hope none of you ever work in any form of healthcare again. Actually, hope none of you ever work again period. Lick pavement for all I care.
I took all of my pets to Porter Pet for years....then they closed, vanished without any notice! I have no way to obtain my pet records!! Years of being a loyal customer!! This is UNACCEPTABLE!!!!

Terrible service. Terrible clinic , Terrible customer service. 10 days ago I took my dog for a check to find out about the growth on her leg and the limping. The doctor seen my pet and took biopsy charged me almost 500$ , said will call with results in 3 days . It took place on Tuesday 11 days ago . They claimed to be open 7 days a week . Today is Friday 29 th , still don’t have the results. Buy the most annoying situation is that I left multiple messages and I keep calling every day and leaving messages. Zero return calls back .Most of the days, they don’t pick up the phone , on Wednesday 8 days later I was able to speak to someone and I was told that someone will call me , but guess what? Nobody has called. And naturally nobody is picking up the phone on Thursday or Friday ( today ) . I love my dog more than anything and I was anxious waiting for the results. I am a medical practitioner and I treated my patients like this , there would be a serious consequences . If you care about your pets. Don’t take your pets to this clinic.

Just found out this place is a a Corporation, no longer private practice owned by vets but a corporation business. Which now make so much sense why the quality of the care for the pets has left this company. Looks like it's been around 5 years now since it was bough?? Not 100% sure but for sure, went from privately own to a corporation owned. How sad.. bring your family members at your own risk but you have been warned.

March 29, 2022 update
The quality oh they veterinarian has gone down. The prices are expensive, and they service is awful. You cant go in, you never meet the vet face to face. All you get is a phone call. I feel like they are just out to charge all they can with out regard to the animal. The left hand doesnt know what the right hand is doing. Vet tells you what the pet needs, your supposed to set appointment with the staff but I dont think they keep notes or communicates with the vet because they never know why your scheduling an appointment with them. They always ask you what is it you needs when your relying they know what they are doing. Just so disappointing, they make me lose faith in vets. Money hungry, which is ok, if only they actualy took care of your family member who needs help.

Don't remember when I wrote this initial review but it was a long time ago, longer than 5years from the year 2023

I've had many cats within my 32 years of life. Some have come and gone. I have brought all most, all of them here and any time I havent was due to emergencies or laziness on my end and I've regretted every time. This place has always given affordable prices, treated me and my little ones with dignity and respect. With kindness and compassion and have made us feel important. They are never to busy to see us which realy counts. I would recommend them to anyone and everyone. I've been coming here since I received my 1st cat at the age of 14 years. I'm sorry its taken me this long to give them the credit due. Thank you all
